discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Leaving this out on purpose. Counting spawns in a unit test would mean mocking `node:child_process`, which breaks the promisified `execFile` (`.child` / `{ stdout }`), or putting a shell-script `git` wrapper on PATH, which won't work on Windows. We try not to add test-only plumbing like that. The process counts were checked against real checkpoints instead: CLI and VS Code sessions on a repo with 3,000 untracked files. main peaked at 3,051 concurrent git processes and 3,046 zombies for one comparison; this branch uses 6 git processes in total per comparison. The existing tests still cover correctness for both the tracked and the third-parent lookups.

Fixed in ac405ed: the SSH listing now runs a small POSIX sh script (folder passed as a positional argument) whose [ -d ] test follows symlinks, so a link to a folder gets the trailing slash and expands like locally; dotfiles and dangling links are still listed. The script is executed for real in project-files.test.ts against a temp folder with a linked folder and a dangling link.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

Valid, added. `skills-cli.test.ts` checks the exported value against core's `package.json`: the devDependency must be an exact `x.y.z` (no tag or range) and `SKILLS_CLI_VERSION` / `SKILLS_CLI_PACKAGE` must equal it. I checked that hardcoding `"skills@latest"` back into the constant makes it fail. The call-site tests keep using the constant, as you suggested.

Fixed. The panel-side check now mirrors the loader: a boolean `disabled` wins, and `enabled: false` only counts when `disabled` is absent. Covered by the new `isFrontmatterDisabled` test and a reconcile test with both flags present.

Valid, and it exposed the real problem: the extension kept its own copy of the SDK's rules for reading a rule's enabled state, and this was the fourth case where the copy disagreed with the SDK. The copy is gone. The Rules panel, both write paths, and the editor now call `parseRuleConfigFromMarkdown` / `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown` from `@cline/core`, so they cannot disagree with what the SDK loads. A file with non-mapping frontmatter (which the SDK loads as having no metadata) is disabled by adding a `disabled: true` block above it, and re-enabling restores it exactly; a comment-only block gets the flag appended inside it. Tests cover both, plus a scratch property check of ~16k generated shapes against the SDK parser as the oracle with zero refusals of loadable files. A file the SDK does not load at all now shows as off, since nothing from it reaches the model.

+import http from "node:http"
+import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net"
+import { Agent, fetch as undiciFetch } from "undici"
+import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
+import { fetchWithoutIdleTimeouts } from "./net"
+
+// A server that answers headers immediately and then stays silent before
+// sending the body, like a local model server processing a large prompt.
+// undici's idle timers tick at 1s resolution, so the silence has to clear a
+// full tick for the control timeout to fire.
+const BODY_DELAY_MS = 2_000
+const CONTROL_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS = 500
+
+describe("fetchWithoutIdleTimeouts", () => {
+	let server: http.Server
+	let url: string
+
+	beforeAll(async () => {
+		server = http.createServer((_req, res) => {
+			res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "text/plain" })
+			res.flushHeaders()
+			setTimeout(() => res.end("first token"), BODY_DELAY_MS)
+		})
+		await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve))
+		url = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}/v1/chat/completions`
+	})
+
+	afterAll(async () => {
+		await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()))
+	})
+
+	it("waits through a silent body where undici's idle timeout would abort", async () => {
+		// Control: the same request through a dispatcher with a short idle
+		// timeout dies, proving the server really is silent long enough.
+		const impatient = new Agent({ bodyTimeout: CONTROL_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS })
+		await expect(undiciFetch(url, { dispatcher: impatient }).then((r) => r.text())).rejects.toThrow()
+		await impatient.close()
+
+		const response = await fetchWithoutIdleTimeouts(url)

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fair point. The test now clears the proxy environment variables before the dispatcher is built and restores them afterwards; verified locally with a bogus http_proxy set.

Valid, fixed in ffb6b03bd3. `preload` no longer goes through `loadForSession`. It records discovery and settings state and imports each path, and the imported copy stays as the spare the first session claims. Test: "keeps the module copy imported by preload for the first session" counts module evaluations: one after preload, still one after the first session, two after the second.

Added two cases: a `tool_call.id` given as a number, which checks the message names `tool_call.id`, and a payload missing four required fields, which checks exactly three are listed. Each one fails if I break the matching part of the formatting (joining the path, or the `slice(0, 3)` limit).

Fixed in 879dfc0553. Native media is extracted before JSON text expansion, so decoded application records are never passed through image extraction. Added regression coverage for image-shaped JSON at the root and inside an MCP text block alongside a real native image. All fields remain in recovery text, and the native attachment stays on the media path. SDK build, core/shared typechecks, and 65 focused tests passed.

Fixed in ab093fb5e. All 13 flat constants are exported again from `@cline/ui/components/mermaid-diagram` as aliases of the current grouped config values (`DIAGRAM_NAMING`, `DIAGRAM_ZOOM`, `MERMAID_FONT`, `PNG_EXPORT`), so the groups stay the single source of truth and the flat names can't drift. A new façade test (tests/diagrams/mermaid/exports.test.ts) imports all 13 names from the entry point and asserts they equal the grouped values; suite is 343/343 green and typecheck passes.
it strips every plural suffix so a Russian catalog missing `_few`/`_many` passes. the catalog is good today but nothing guards it.
agent: guarded in 3d7457208 — new test requires every plural group to carry exactly the locale's CLDR cardinal categories

Valid, thanks. The wire-level test now runs the same assertions through `doStream` as well as `doGenerate`, for both `cline` and `cline-pass`, and checks the request is a streaming one. Removing the headers from the Cline provider fails all four cases.

The helper now asserts, for `unlisted`, that the id is absent from `gateway.listModels("bedrock")`, so a catalog sync that adds the id fails the case instead of silently testing the listed path. Verified it bites by pointing the case at a catalogued id, which fails against the 167-entry Bedrock list.

Fixed in 371b586c3 — now uses `fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../dist/index.js", import.meta.url))` from `node:url`, so Windows drive letters and percent-encoded spaces resolve to a real filesystem path.

agent feedback: The first three recovery tests cover the feature's main promises well: successful retry, truncation again, and nothing to compact. The tests from here onward mostly protect detailed telemetry behavior for listener errors, hooks, empty responses, and tool-call variants that the run loop already owns. If the telemetry contract is simplified to whether compaction/retry completed, I think these extra cases and much of their supporting implementation can be removed while preserving the important behavioral coverage.
correct. dropped.

Valid — fixed, test-first: both `stop` and `max-tokens` empty retries reproduced exactly this (`Model returned empty response`, truncated turn gone). An empty retry is no more a replacement than an aborted or errored one, so it now keeps the truncated turn and lets the loop surface the max-tokens error, matching the nothing-to-compact path. Also added a table-driven test over the full retry-outcome matrix (every finish reason × text / tool call / empty / provider-executed activity) asserting the partial answer is never silently dropped and the loop is never handed an empty turn — all 20 cells pass.
